sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: If you listened to our show last year, you may have heard the voice of Elliot Kalin,
sentences.zh: 如果你去年听过我们的节目，可能听到过埃利奥特·卡林的声音，

sentences.en: who was my co-host for a series we did on the book The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 他是我制作的关于《权力掮客》一书系列节目的联合主持人。

sentences.en: And as far as I'm concerned, Elliot was the perfect co-hoSt.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，埃利奥特是完美的联合主持人。

sentences.en: He's smart, knowledgeable, easy to talk to, and he's also very, very funny.
sentences.zh: 他聪明、博学、健谈，而且非常、非常幽默。

sentences.en: Because when he's not moonlighting at 99PI, Elliot is a professional comedy writer.
sentences.zh: 因为当他不以《99%隐形》为副业时，埃利奥特是一位专业的喜剧编剧。

sentences.en: And over the years, he has written comedy in just about every medium there is.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他几乎在所有现存的媒介上都写过喜剧。

sentences.en: He worked for over a decade at The Daily Show with Jon Stewart,
sentences.zh: 他在乔恩·斯图尔特的《每日秀》工作了十多年，

sentences.en: where he eventually became the show's head writer.
sentences.zh: 最终成为了该节目的首席编剧。

sentences.en: He did stand-up, he writes comic books,
sentences.zh: 他表演过单口喜剧，写过漫画书，

sentences.en: and currently he is the co-host of the original bad movie podcast, The Flophouse,
sentences.zh: 目前是原创烂片播客《Flophouse》的联合主持人，

sentences.en: and the showrunner for the forthcoming Netflix Ghostbusters animated series.
sentences.zh: 还是Netflix即将推出的《捉鬼敢死队》动画系列的剧集主管。

sentences.en: We want to have Elliot back on the show because he has now written a book of his own.
sentences.zh: 我们想请埃利奥特回到节目中，因为他现在写了一本自己的书。

sentences.en: Not so much about his career, but about his craft.
sentences.zh: 与其说是关于他的职业生涯，不如说是关于他的创作技艺。

sentences.en: He says, when you write jokes for a living, it takes a lot more than just having a good sense of humor.
sentences.zh: 他说，当你以写笑话为生时，需要的不仅仅是幽默感。

sentences.en: Instead, you have to have a system.
sentences.zh: 相反，你必须拥有一套系统。

sentences.en: The book is called Joke Farming, How to Write Comedy and Other Nonsense.
sentences.zh: 这本书叫《笑话耕作：如何撰写喜剧及其他胡言乱语》。

sentences.en: And he's here to talk about it with us.
sentences.zh: 他今天来到这里，和我们一起谈谈这本书。

sentences.en: Elliot Kalin, it is so nice to have you back.
sentences.zh: 埃利奥特·卡林，很高兴你能回来。

sentences.en: Thank you, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: It's great to be back.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能回来。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me on to promote a book that I make some money off of.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你邀请我来宣传一本我能从中赚点钱的书。

sentences.en: After we did so much to put some money in Robert Caro's pockets,
sentences.zh: 在我们为罗伯特·卡罗的口袋里塞了那么多钱之后，

sentences.en: I appreciate my getting a shot at it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激自己也能有机会赚点钱。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So let's get, you know, down to the basics, the very, very beginning.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们回归基础，从最最开始说起吧。

sentences.en: You know, what on earth made you think that you could write jokes for a living?
sentences.zh: 你到底是什么时候觉得你可以靠写笑话为生的？

sentences.en: The great thing about writing jokes for a living is that
sentences.zh: 以写笑话为生的好处在于，

sentences.en: less that you need someone to tell you you can do it,
sentences.zh: 与其说你需要别人告诉你你能做到，

sentences.en: and more that no one can tell you not to do it.
sentences.zh: 不如说没人能阻止你去做。

sentences.en: And it helped that I grew up also watching television in the early 1990s
sentences.zh: 而且我成长在20世纪90年代初，当时我也在看电视，

sentences.en: when there was still a lot of stand-up comedy on television in particular.
sentences.zh: 那时电视上特别是有很多单口喜剧节目。

sentences.en: Like, you and I, I'm a little older than you,
sentences.zh: 就像你和我，虽然我比你大一点，

sentences.en: but there was this phase of, like, cable television
sentences.zh: 但当时有线电视有一个阶段，

sentences.en: where all of a sudden you saw somebody standing in front of a brick wall,
sentences.zh: 你会突然看到有人站在砖墙前，

sentences.en: you know, like, as part of television, you know?
sentences.zh: 你知道，作为电视节目的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: And now we live in a world where it feels like there's more comedy than not comedy.
sentences.zh: 现在我们生活在一个感觉喜剧无处不在的世界里。

sentences.en: So now it seems quaint, but it felt like there was so much comedy around that
sentences.zh: 所以现在看来这很古怪，但当时感觉周围有那么多喜剧，

sentences.en: this was something you could do.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一件你可以做的事情。

sentences.en: And so I very foolishly somehow managed to achieve the lucky breaks to succeed at doing it,
sentences.zh: 于是我非常愚蠢地以某种方式获得了成功的幸运机会，

sentences.en: which baffles me and my family to this very day.
sentences.zh: 这至今让我和我的家人感到困惑。

sentences.en: But what I'm curious about is, like, you got into this because
sentences.zh: 但我好奇的是，你进入这一行是因为

sentences.en: the adults in your life told you you're a naturally funny person.
sentences.zh: 你生命中的成年人告诉你，你是一个天生幽默的人。

sentences.en: You're a person that just makes people laugh.
sentences.zh: 你是一个能让人发笑的人。

sentences.en: But that is not enough if you need to produce The Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 但如果你需要制作《每日秀》，这还不够。

sentences.en: You can't just be naturally funny.
sentences.zh: 你不能仅仅是天生幽默。

sentences.en: It is a job.
sentences.zh: 这是一份工作。

sentences.en: And you cultivated this thing called joke farming
sentences.zh: 你培养了这种叫做“笑话耕作”的东西，

sentences.en: as a way to produce all the jokes that you have to do for something like The Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 作为一种为你必须为《每日秀》这类节目创作所有笑话的方法。

sentences.en: Can you talk about joke farming and how you sort of developed it as a discipline?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈笑话耕作以及你是如何将其发展为一种纪律的吗？

sentences.en: I feel like the difference between being a funny person and being a comedy professional
sentences.zh: 我觉得成为一个幽默的人和成为一名喜剧专业人士的区别在于，

sentences.en: is the ability to be funny not just spontaneously,
sentences.zh: 不仅能自发地幽默，

sentences.en: not just for whoever you're talking to,
sentences.zh: 不仅是对着你正在交谈的人幽默，

sentences.en: but to be funny on demand in a professional manner when it needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 而且能在需要的时候以专业的方式按需幽默。

sentences.en: You can't wait for inspiration to strike.
sentences.zh: 你不能等待灵感降临。

sentences.en: It has to be a reliable thing that you can go to when you need it,
sentences.zh: 它必须是你需要时可以调用的可靠工具，

sentences.en: and you can command it to a certain extent rather than letting it command you.
sentences.zh: 你可以在一定程度上驾驭它，而不是让它驾驭你。

sentences.en: And so when I was working at The Daily Show,
sentences.zh: 所以当我在《每日秀》工作时，

sentences.en: I worked with a lot of writers, and I was like this too,
sentences.zh: 我和很多编剧一起工作，我也曾是那样，

sentences.en: where at first it was writing by gut.
sentences.zh: 起初是凭直觉写作。

sentences.en: You're writing the thing that you think is funny in the moment,
sentences.zh: 你写下你当下觉得好笑的东西，

sentences.en: and you spend a lot of time staring into space when something isn't coming to you.
sentences.zh: 当你想不出东西时，你会花很多时间盯着虚空发呆。

sentences.en: But when you're in an office and they're like,
sentences.zh: 但当你在办公室里，他们说，

sentences.en: it's 9 o'clock and your script is due at 10.30.
sentences.zh: 现在是9点，你的剧本10点半就要交了。

sentences.en: You can't do that.
sentences.zh: 你不能那样做。

sentences.en: And so I knew I had to write a lot of jokes really faSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道我必须非常快地写出很多笑话。

sentences.en: And I should define a joke as anything that is created in order to make someone laugh.
sentences.zh: 我应该把笑话定义为任何为了让人发笑而创作的东西。

sentences.en: That to me is a joke.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就是笑话。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And if I'm not feeling funny that day, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 如果我那天感觉不到幽默，那没关系。

sentences.en: The show still needs it.
sentences.zh: 节目仍然需要它。

sentences.en: And the show needs a lot of jokes,
sentences.zh: 节目需要很多笑话，

sentences.en: and it needs me to write them in, if I'm lucky, two hours, often less than that.
sentences.zh: 而且需要我在两小时内写出来，如果幸运的话，通常时间更短。

sentences.en: And so I started talking to myself about what is the unconscious process that my mind goes through
sentences.zh: 所以我开始对自己进行剖析，当我随口想出一个笑话时，

sentences.en: when I am coming up with a joke off the top of my head.
sentences.zh: 我的大脑经历了什么样的潜意识过程。

sentences.en: I need to verbalize it.
sentences.zh: 我需要把它口语化。

sentences.en: I need to be able to articulate to myself so that I can then replicate it as a real
sentences.zh: 我需要能够向自己清晰地表达出来，这样我才能把它复制成一个真正的、

sentences.en: deliberate process that I can force myself to go through.
sentences.zh: 我可以强迫自己去执行的刻意过程。

sentences.en: And did you go through this exercise of figuring this out, verbalizing it at the time,
sentences.zh: 你当时是否经历了这种弄清楚并将其口语化的练习，

sentences.en: or is this something that you did writing the book?
sentences.zh: 还是这是你在写书时才做的？

sentences.en: Or is this, you know, like, did you?
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，你是怎么做的？

sentences.en: Oh, no, this is something I did at the time.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，这是我当时就做的事情。

sentences.en: This is, I said to myself, I need to free myself from being chained to inspiration,
sentences.zh: 我对自己说，我需要让自己从被灵感束缚中解放出来，

sentences.en: basically, which is something I can't control.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是我无法控制的事情。

sentences.en: And so I want to have a process where you can take any subject,
sentences.zh: 所以我想要一个过程，你可以拿任何主题，

sentences.en: and you can go through the steps of that process and then come out with a joke on the other end.
sentences.zh: 然后按照那个过程的步骤走，最后就能得出一个笑话。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I want to get across in the book is that you don't have to use my process,
sentences.zh: 我想在书中传达的一点是，你不必使用我的过程，

sentences.en: but it's good to have a process.
sentences.zh: 但拥有一个过程是件好事。

sentences.en: And your process should mimic your way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 你的过程应该模仿你的思维方式。

sentences.en: It should fit your needs, your voice, how you most comfortably write.
sentences.zh: 它应该适合你的需求、你的声音，以及你最舒适的写作方式。

sentences.en: But whatever that process is, it should be something that you know the steps of so that at those times when you don't have inspiration,
sentences.zh: 但无论那个过程是什么，它都应该是你了解步骤的东西，这样在那些没有灵感的时候，

sentences.en: but you need to produce a joke, you can do it.
sentences.zh: 但你需要创作一个笑话时，你就能做到。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's talk about some of that processing and how the Daily Show process morphed into your own process that you described.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们来谈谈其中的一些处理过程，以及《每日秀》的过程是如何演变成你所描述的你自己的过程的。

sentences.en: I mean, for copyright and patent purposes, this is my own original process, you know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，出于版权和专利的目的，这是我原创的过程，你知道的。

sentences.en: I'm sure there's influences, but let's not give them too much credit.
sentences.zh: 我相信肯定有影响，但我们别给它们太多的功劳。

sentences.en: No, I feel the thing I should say also about the work in the Daily Show, I don't want it to sound like I'm a genius who came up with all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得关于《每日秀》的工作，我也应该说，我不想听起来像是我是一个想出所有这些东西的天才。

sentences.en: You know, this was very much me being taught and led by the people I was very lucky to be working with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很大程度上是我被那些我有幸与之共事的人教导和引导的结果。

sentences.en: So your day at the Daily Show starts.
sentences.zh: 那么你在《每日秀》的一天开始了。

sentences.en: There's lots of news.
sentences.zh: 有很多新闻。

sentences.en: Some of it is hard news to figure out how to make comedy about.
sentences.zh: 其中一些很难弄清楚如何将其转化为喜剧。

sentences.en: Some of it maybe is super easy to make comedy about.
sentences.zh: 其中一些可能非常容易转化为喜剧。

sentences.en: Some of it's very easy.
sentences.zh: 有些非常容易。

sentences.en: There was one time there was a stadium that got built somewhere and from above it looked like a vagina.
sentences.zh: 有一次，某个地方建了一个体育场，从上面看它像个阴道。

sentences.en: And it was a very easy one to write jokes about.
sentences.zh: 写关于它的笑话非常容易。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so could you take us through the joke farming process with a joke from the Daily Show?
sentences.zh: 那么你能带我们通过《每日秀》的一个笑话来了解笑话耕作的过程吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So the first thing I would have to do is consider who is telling this joke?
sentences.zh: 所以我首先要考虑的是，谁在讲这个笑话？

sentences.en: Who is the joke teller whose voice is it?
sentences.zh: 谁是讲笑话的人，这是谁的声音？

sentences.en: Which in the case of the Daily Show when I was there would have been Jon Stewart.
sentences.zh: 我在《每日秀》工作时，那个人就是乔恩·斯图尔特。

sentences.en: He's the host of the show.
sentences.zh: 他是节目的主持人。

sentences.en: He's going to say all the jokes.
sentences.zh: 所有的笑话都由他来说。

sentences.en: Then I would try to say to myself, what is the point of this joke?
sentences.zh: 然后我会试着问自己，这个笑话的重点是什么？

sentences.en: And by point, I mean what is the message I'm trying to get across in this joke?
sentences.zh: 我所说的重点，是指我想在这个笑话中传达的信息是什么？

sentences.en: What's the meaning of it?
sentences.zh: 它的含义是什么？

sentences.en: Not necessarily the funny thing about it.
sentences.zh: 不一定是关于它的好笑之处。

sentences.en: In fact, often it's the least funny part of the joke.
sentences.zh: 事实上，通常它是笑话中最不好笑的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so an example that I was always very proud of myself too much, so much people would say, is a joke that I wrote for the Daily Show in 2015.
sentences.zh: 我一直对自己感到太自豪的一个例子，以至于人们会说，是我在2015年为《每日秀》写的一个笑话。

sentences.en: There had been a terrorist attack in France, and the United States sent the then Secretary of State John Kerry on a goodwill visit.
sentences.zh: 法国发生了恐怖袭击，美国派当时的国务卿约翰·克里进行了友好访问。

sentences.en: Secretary of State John Kerry is on a charm offensive this morning in Paris.
sentences.zh: 国务卿约翰·克里今天早上在巴黎进行魅力攻势。

sentences.en: And the thing about John Kerry is at the time he was famous for being very boring and stiff, just a slow-talking, like a statue of a man.
sentences.zh: 关于约翰·克里的事情是，当时他以非常无聊和僵硬而闻名，只是一个说话缓慢的人，就像一个人的雕像。

sentences.en: He's more statue than man.
sentences.zh: 他更像是一座雕像而不是一个人。

sentences.en: I would like to say directly to the people of Paris and of all of France that each and every American stands with you today,
sentences.zh: 我想直接对巴黎和全法国的人民说，每一个美国人都与你们站在一起，

sentences.en: both to the cause of confronting extremism and in the cause which the extremists fear so much.
sentences.zh: 既是为了对抗极端主义的事业，也是为了极端分子所恐惧的事业。

sentences.en: And the first point that jumps into your head is this is the guy you're sending on a goodwill visit, this guy who is very boring and very unpersonable.
sentences.zh: 你脑子里跳出的第一个重点是，这就是你派去进行友好访问的人，这个非常无聊且非常没有人格魅力的人。

sentences.en: But that seemed very obvious.
sentences.zh: 但这看起来太明显了。

sentences.en: There had to be something less obvious than John Kerry is boring,
sentences.zh: 一定有比“约翰·克里很无聊”更不明显的东西，

sentences.en: which at this point of the Daily Show I think we had told roughly 700,000 million jokes about John Kerry being boring.
sentences.zh: 在《每日秀》的这一点上，我想我们已经讲了大约7000亿个关于约翰·克里很无聊的笑话了。

sentences.en: So in looking through the material that we had been given by the researchers and segment producers for this piece,
sentences.zh: 所以在查看研究人员和片段制作人为这段内容提供给我们的材料时，

sentences.en: I found this Wolf Blitzer clip where he's reminding us that John Kerry is this enormous Francophile.
sentences.zh: 我发现了这个沃尔夫·布利策的片段，他提醒我们约翰·克里是一个巨大的亲法派。

sentences.en: He loves France.
sentences.zh: 他热爱法国。

sentences.en: John Kerry speaks French, loves France, studied in France.
sentences.zh: 约翰·克里会说法语，热爱法国，在法国学习过。

sentences.en: So the point I decided to go with for this joke is the world's stiffest, least kind of cool man loves everything about the world's sexiest country.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定为这个笑话选择的重点是，世界上最僵硬、最不酷的人热爱世界上最性感国家的一切。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But that's a point.
sentences.zh: 但这只是一个重点。

sentences.en: It's not a – if I say it like that, it's not funny.
sentences.zh: 它不是一个——如果我那样说，它并不好笑。

sentences.en: That's not a joke.
sentences.zh: 那不是一个笑话。

sentences.en: No, it's not a joke.
sentences.zh: 不，那不是笑话。

sentences.en: It's just me stating a true fact.
sentences.zh: 那只是我在陈述一个事实。

sentences.en: And so I have to develop a premise to go around it.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须围绕它发展一个前提。

sentences.en: And a premise is essentially what is the little story that you're going to tell this joke through that gets close to the point but not so close that you're just saying it so that the audience can make a little leap in their minds and they can get it.
sentences.zh: 前提本质上是你将通过它讲述这个笑话的小故事，它接近重点，但又不会太近，以至于你只是直接说出来，这样观众可以在脑海中进行一个小小的跳跃，他们就能明白。

sentences.en: Like you're setting up a scenario so they will arrive to the point without you telling them the point of the joke.
sentences.zh: 就像你在设置一个场景，这样他们就会在你不告诉他们笑话重点的情况下得出结论。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And one way I like to think about premises is kind of like what if scenarios.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢考虑前提的一种方式是类似于“如果……会怎样”的场景。

sentences.en: And so I said to myself, what if John Kerry loves French things so much that as long as the word French is in there, he loves it.
sentences.zh: 所以我对自己说，如果约翰·克里如此热爱法国事物，以至于只要里面有“法国”这个词，他就喜欢，会怎样？

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: French fries, French kissing, French horns.
sentences.zh: 炸薯条（French fries）、法式热吻（French kissing）、法国号（French horns）。

sentences.en: And it bakes in the second point that is unrelated to the story that I was covering but it's kind of a funny point still to me, which is there's all this stuff that's not French.
sentences.zh: 而且这还巩固了第二点，虽然与我正在讲述的故事无关，但对我来说仍然很有趣，那就是有很多东西其实并不是法国的。

sentences.en: But we call it French, which is really fun.
sentences.zh: 但我们却叫它“法国”什么什么，这真的很有意思。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I've got the premise.
sentences.zh: 所以，前提我已经有了。

sentences.en: John Kerry loves everything with French in the name.
sentences.zh: 约翰·克里喜欢名字里带“法国”的一切。

sentences.en: Now I need structure.
sentences.zh: 现在我需要结构。

sentences.en: And structure is literally the mechanical construction of the joke.
sentences.zh: 结构实际上就是笑话的机械构造。

sentences.en: How you release each piece of information one step after another in order.
sentences.zh: 即你如何按顺序一步步释放每一条信息。

sentences.en: So you walk the audience right up to the very edge of the point where they can then make the leap on their own and they land in the joke.
sentences.zh: 你要引导观众走到那个点的边缘，让他们自己完成最后的跳跃，然后落入笑话的包袱中。

sentences.en: So in writing this John Kerry joke, I started riffing on Wolf Lister's cadence.
sentences.zh: 所以在写这个约翰·克里的笑话时，我开始模仿沃尔夫·利斯特的语调。

sentences.en: John Kerry speaks French, loves France, studied in France.
sentences.zh: 约翰·克里会说法语，热爱法国，曾在法国学习。

sentences.en: I wanted to continue that cadence in a kind of a list but where John makes it a question and answer thing.
sentences.zh: 我想用一种列表的形式延续那种语调，但让约翰把它变成一种问答形式。

sentences.en: Instead of saying he loves French fries, he loves French bulldogs.
sentences.zh: 与其说他喜欢炸薯条，不如说他喜欢法国斗牛犬。

sentences.en: Instead it's favorite type of fries.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是，最喜欢的薯条种类。

sentences.en: Favorite type of fries.
sentences.zh: 最喜欢的薯条种类。

sentences.en: And the audience fills in French and he says French.
sentences.zh: 观众填上“法国”，他说“法国”。

sentences.en: Favorite type of bulldog.
sentences.zh: 最喜欢的斗牛犬种类。

sentences.en: Audience fills in French.
sentences.zh: 观众填上“法国”。

sentences.en: French.
sentences.zh: “法国”。

sentences.en: And when you're structuring a joke, you want to do what's called heightening.
sentences.zh: 当你构建一个笑话时，你要做所谓的“强化”。

sentences.en: You want to escalate it from the kind of least funny one, the least exaggerated one to the most exaggerated one.
sentences.zh: 你要从最不好笑、最不夸张的开始，逐渐升级到最夸张的。

sentences.en: And then you move on to more dramatic examples or sillier examples.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以转向更戏剧化或更荒谬的例子。

sentences.en: Favorite kind of me, French.
sentences.zh: 最喜欢的我，法国。

sentences.en: And so I've now established the pattern.
sentences.zh: 现在我已经确立了这种模式。

sentences.en: French, French, French.
sentences.zh: 法国、法国、法国。

sentences.en: It could go on forever.
sentences.zh: 这可以没完没了地进行下去。

sentences.en: There's so many French things.
sentences.zh: 有太多法国相关的东西了。

sentences.en: But then at the end, I want to subvert that pattern.
sentences.zh: 但在最后，我想颠覆这种模式。

sentences.en: I want to disrupt it.
sentences.zh: 我想打破它。

sentences.en: And so I was like, what if there's something where the answer could be French but then it isn't French?
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，如果有一个答案听起来应该是“法国”，但实际上却不是“法国”的东西会怎样？

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好的，好的。

sentences.en: And so there's a kind of mustard called French's mustard.
sentences.zh: 有一种芥末酱叫“法国牌”芥末酱（French's mustard）。

sentences.en: And John Kerry, at the time famously, was married to one of the heirs of the Heinz condiment fortune.
sentences.zh: 而约翰·克里当时很有名的一点是，他娶了亨氏调味品财富的继承人之一。

sentences.en: So I could say, favorite mustard.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以说，最喜欢的芥末酱。

sentences.en: And the audience expects the answer to be French.
sentences.zh: 观众会期待答案是“法国”。

sentences.en: And then John's going to say, Heinz.
sentences.zh: 然后约翰会说，“亨氏”。

sentences.en: Repernizes marriage over mustard.
sentences.zh: 为了芥末酱而重申婚姻。

sentences.en: And so you've taken a joke that's specifically about John Kerry.
sentences.zh: 这样你就把一个专门针对约翰·克里的笑话，

sentences.en: You've made it about, there are a lot of things called French.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个关于“有很多东西叫法国”的笑话。

sentences.en: And then you've taken it back around to being a joke that only works for John Kerry because only John Kerry is married to a Heinz.
sentences.zh: 然后你又把它绕回来，变成了一个只有约翰·克里才好笑的笑话，因为只有约翰·克里娶了亨氏家族的人。

sentences.en: Okay, yes.
sentences.zh: 好的，没错。

sentences.en: And I think the process of working on that took probably less time than it took to describe it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得构思这个的过程可能比描述它花的时间还要短。

sentences.en: You know, because I was like, here are the steps that I'm going through.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为我当时想，这就是我要经历的步骤。

sentences.en: And I could design this joke so much faster than I would have otherwise if I was just sitting here trying to think of something to come out of the blue, you know.
sentences.zh: 我可以比平时更快地设计出这个笑话，而不是坐在这里试图凭空想出点什么，你知道的。

sentences.en: So, but outside of The Daily Show, I know your book has a lot of examples from, you know, from the world of comedy at large.
sentences.zh: 那么，除了《每日秀》，我知道你的书里有很多来自整个喜剧界的例子。

sentences.en: What are other good examples of somebody using structure to subvert expectation?
sentences.zh: 还有哪些利用结构来颠覆预期的好例子？

sentences.en: So most people are familiar, I think, with the kind of structure that you would call set up punchline.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人都熟悉那种被称为“铺垫加包袱”的结构。

sentences.en: And one of the examples I use in the book is a joke by Rita Rudner, who I think is one of the greatest stand-ups of all time.
sentences.zh: 我在书中使用的一个例子是丽塔·鲁德纳的笑话，我认为她是史上最伟大的单口喜剧演员之一。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I grew up with her.
sentences.zh: 我是看着她的表演长大的。

sentences.en: She was one of the stand-outs of the 80s.
sentences.zh: 她是80年代的杰出人物之一。

sentences.en: She's amazing, yeah.
sentences.zh: 她太棒了，没错。

sentences.en: And one of her first jokes, she says,
sentences.zh: 在她的一个早期笑话里，她说：

sentences.en: It's going to be a long time for me for children.
sentences.zh: “我生孩子还得等很久。”

sentences.en: I'm very single.
sentences.zh: “我还是单身。”

sentences.en: I was going with someone for a few years, but we broke up.
sentences.zh: “我曾和某人交往了几年，但我们分手了。”

sentences.en: It's one of those things.
sentences.zh: “就是那种事。”

sentences.en: He wanted to get married, and I didn't want him to.
sentences.zh: “他想结婚，但我不想让他结。”

sentences.en: But that structure of, here's a piece of information, and now I'm going to subvert it slightly with the punchline.
sentences.zh: 但那种结构是：这里有一条信息，现在我要用包袱稍微颠覆一下它。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to say, I broke up with my boyfriend.
sentences.zh: 我不会说“我和我男朋友分手了”。

sentences.en: He wanted to get married, but he married his other girlfriend.
sentences.zh: “他想结婚，但他和别的女朋友结婚了。”

sentences.en: Like, that's not a funny way to say it.
sentences.zh: 那样说一点也不好笑。

sentences.en: But you're surprising the audience by providing an answer that is ideally logical, but not in the way that the audience originally thought it was going to be.
sentences.zh: 但你通过提供一个在逻辑上理想、但不是观众最初预想的那种答案，给观众带来了惊喜。

sentences.en: I think it's an amazing joke.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个很棒的笑话。

sentences.en: Because the sentence that subverts expectations,
sentences.zh: 因为那个颠覆预期的句子，

sentences.en: All the meaning of the joke relies on the word him.
sentences.zh: 笑话的所有含义都依赖于“他”（him）这个词。

sentences.en: Yes, and I would say it is a brilliant joke to me because so much of it is packed in that word.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会说这对我来说是一个绝妙的笑话，因为太多的含义都浓缩在那个词里了。

sentences.en: And the fewer number of words that you can use to deliver a joke, the fewer number of details you can provide, usually the better.
sentences.zh: 而且你用来讲笑话的词越少，提供的细节越少，通常效果就越好。

sentences.en: You don't want to confuse the audience and with the clearest, most precise word that you can use.
sentences.zh: 你不想让观众感到困惑，要用你能用到的最清晰、最精确的词。

sentences.en: And so there might be that moment where the audience takes a short second to understand it and to complete it for themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以可能会有那么一瞬间，观众需要花一秒钟去理解并自己补全它。

sentences.en: But that's the moment where the joke lives, that beautiful moment there.
sentences.zh: 但那正是笑话的生命所在，那美妙的一刻。

sentences.en: In the book, you say that in your joke writing process, there's other elements to a joke that you'd like to consider beyond the point, the premise, and the structure.
sentences.zh: 在书中，你说在你的笑话创作过程中，除了核心点、前提和结构之外，还有其他因素需要考虑。

sentences.en: So after you've figured out that core logic, what comes next?
sentences.zh: 那么在弄清楚核心逻辑之后，接下来是什么？

sentences.en: So then we get into what I would call the fiddling with the joke, where you work on the tone of it, kind of like what emotional implications are you trying to get into it?
sentences.zh: 接下来就是我所说的“打磨笑话”，你要处理它的基调，比如你想在其中注入什么样的情感暗示？

sentences.en: Are you speaking with sincerity or insincerity?
sentences.zh: 你是真诚地还是不真诚地在说？

sentences.en: What level of irony are you bringing to this?
sentences.zh: 你给它带来了什么程度的讽刺？

sentences.en: What level of aggression towards the audience or towards the subject of the joke are you bringing?
sentences.zh: 你对观众或笑话的主题带来了什么程度的攻击性？

sentences.en: And it's kind of like when you're speaking at a wedding where you're trying to balance the sincerity of your feelings towards the couple that are getting married with the insincerity of the kind of ribbing that you're doing of them.
sentences.zh: 这就像在婚礼上发言，你试图平衡你对新婚夫妇的真诚情感，和你对他们的那种调侃的不真诚感。

sentences.en: So give me an example of tone and tone management when you're doing a joke.
sentences.zh: 那么给我举一个你在讲笑话时处理基调的例子。

sentences.en: So Don Rickles, for instance, who Don Rickles, for the younger members of the listenership, if they don't know,
sentences.zh: 比如唐·里克斯，对于年轻的听众，如果他们不知道的话，

sentences.en: Don Rickles was the master of insult comedy that was just so aggressively over-the-top hostile that you could not take it seriously as real, actual hostility.
sentences.zh: 唐·里克斯是侮辱喜剧的大师，他的表演极具攻击性，以至于你根本不会把它当作真实、实际的敌意。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗？

sentences.en: His wife and your wife have the same name, Frank's wife and your wife?
sentences.zh: 他老婆和你老婆名字一样，弗兰克的老婆和你老婆？

sentences.en: What are you, a detective?
sentences.zh: 你是侦探吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm a detective.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是侦探。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, you come up with these remarks.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你能想出这些话来。

sentences.en: They have the same name.
sentences.zh: 她们名字一样。

sentences.en: Don't say.
sentences.zh: 别说了。

sentences.en: Whereas sometimes the more deadpan you are, like with a comedian like Stephen Wright, who I think is a master, but his stuff is so deadpan that you're like, well,
sentences.zh: 而有时你越是面无表情，比如像斯蒂芬·赖特这样的喜剧演员，我认为他是大师，但他的东西太冷幽默了，你会觉得，嗯，

sentences.en: obviously he didn't really do these things.
sentences.zh: 显然他并没有真的做过这些事。

sentences.en: I called the wrong number today.
sentences.zh: 我今天打错了电话。

sentences.en: I said, hello, is Joey there?
sentences.zh: 我说，喂，乔伊在吗？

sentences.en: And a woman answered.
sentences.zh: 一个女人接了电话。

sentences.en: She said, yes, he is.
sentences.zh: 她说，是的，他在。

sentences.en: I said, can I speak to him, please?
sentences.zh: 我说，能让他接电话吗？

sentences.en: She said, no, he can't talk right now.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，他现在不能说话。

sentences.en: He's only two months old.
sentences.zh: 他才两个月大。

sentences.en: I said, all right, I'll wait.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我等他。

sentences.en: I mean, who is telling the joke is it's maybe not as important as the joke itself, but it's like up there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，谁在讲这个笑话可能不如笑话本身重要，但也差不多了。

sentences.en: It's who is telling the joke is the first piece of information that the audience gets about the joke.
sentences.zh: 谁在讲笑话是观众关于这个笑话得到的第一条信息。

sentences.en: Who is this person?
sentences.zh: 这个人是谁？

sentences.en: What do I assume their perspective that they're bringing to it is?
sentences.zh: 我假设他们带入其中的视角是什么？

sentences.en: And in the book, I talk about kind of like stand-up persona and how it can help become the context for the tone of a joke.
sentences.zh: 在书中，我谈到了单口喜剧的人设，以及它如何帮助成为笑话基调的背景。

sentences.en: And an example of this that I use in the book is Charlie Hill, who is another great comic, who is a member of the Oneida Nation.
sentences.zh: 我在书中用的一个例子是查理·希尔，他是另一位伟大的喜剧演员，是奥奈达部落的成员。

sentences.en: A lot of you white people have never seen an Indian do stand-up comedy before, you know.
sentences.zh: 你们很多白人以前从没见过印第安人表演单口喜剧，你知道的。

sentences.en: Like for so long, you probably thought that Indians never had a sense of humor, you know.
sentences.zh: 好像很长一段时间以来，你们可能认为印第安人从来没有幽默感，你知道的。

sentences.en: We never thought you were too funny either.
sentences.zh: 我们也从没觉得你们有多好笑。

sentences.en: He was on a talk show in the 70s, and they asked him if he ever played Cowboy and Indians,
sentences.zh: 他在70年代上过一个脱口秀节目，他们问他是否玩过“牛仔和印第安人”，

sentences.en: which I hope was a setup that he provided for them and not an actual question that they were asking him.
sentences.zh: 我希望这是他为他们提供的铺垫，而不是他们真的问他的问题。

sentences.en: And he said, no, we never played Cowboys and Indians, but we did play Nazis and Jews.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，我们从不玩“牛仔和印第安人”，但我们玩过“纳粹和犹太人”。

sentences.en: The rules are the same.
sentences.zh: 规则是一样的。

sentences.en: And that's a harsh – I love that joke.
sentences.zh: 那是一个尖锐的——我喜欢那个笑话。

sentences.en: That's a hard joke.
sentences.zh: 那是一个沉重的笑话。

sentences.en: But it's a – coming from someone who is bringing the perspective of a Native American and indigenous person, it means a certain thing.
sentences.zh: 但它——来自一个带着美洲原住民和土著人视角的人，它意味着某种东西。

sentences.en: It is not a joke that means to make a joke about the ideas of Nazis killing Jews.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一个旨在拿纳粹杀害犹太人的想法开玩笑的笑话。

sentences.en: It is instead about reframing this childhood game that makes light of genocide in the light of another genocide that the audience recognizes, but in a funny way, as a funny joke.
sentences.zh: 它反而是为了重构这个把种族灭绝当儿戏的童年游戏，将其置于观众所认知的另一种种族灭绝的光照下，但以一种有趣的方式，作为一个有趣的笑话。

sentences.en: And the fact that it's coming from Charlie Hill means we understand what he's getting at.
sentences.zh: 而且它出自查理·希尔之口，意味着我们理解他想表达什么。

sentences.en: And this leads us to the audience, which is like the completion of the joke, which is essentially like the last part and the most important part.
sentences.zh: 这把我们引向了观众，他们就像是笑话的完成者，这本质上是最后一部分，也是最重要的一部分。

sentences.en: It's the most important – unfortunately, it's the most important part.
sentences.zh: 这是最重要——不幸的是，这是最重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And like nobody – you can't tell a joke on your own.
sentences.zh: 就像没人——你不能独自讲笑话。

sentences.en: Like the audience provides the most important part of the joke, which is the person laughing at the joke.
sentences.zh: 观众提供了笑话中最重要的一部分，那就是那个对笑话发笑的人。

sentences.en: And there's something very depressingly humbling about the idea that like you don't get to decide ultimately if your work is funny or not.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常令人沮丧且谦卑的想法，那就是你最终无法决定你的作品是否好笑。

sentences.en: Like the audience gets to decide, and if they're not laughing, then you failed them.
sentences.zh: 观众说了算，如果他们不笑，那你就是辜负了他们。

sentences.en: But they also – the audience wants to laugh.
sentences.zh: 但他们也——观众是想笑的。

sentences.en: And that was such a big thing for me when I was performing stand-up was remembering the audience is not there to get mad at me.
sentences.zh: 这对我表演单口喜剧时非常重要，要记住观众不是来找我麻烦的。

sentences.en: They're not challenging me.
sentences.zh: 他们不是在挑战我。

sentences.en: They might be a little bit, but they want the joke writer or the performer to succeed because it's more fun for them.
sentences.zh: 他们可能有一点点，但他们希望笑话创作者或表演者成功，因为这对他们来说更有趣。

sentences.en: And you want to succeed by maybe challenging what they're going to laugh at a little bit, but not challenging it so much that you're deliberately bombing.
sentences.zh: 你想通过挑战他们会笑的东西来获得成功，但不要挑战得太过分，以至于故意冷场。

sentences.en: There are some comedians who love to bomb.
sentences.zh: 有些喜剧演员喜欢冷场。

sentences.en: It's very fun if you're a comedian to watch another comedian bomb, but only because then you become the audience.
sentences.zh: 如果你是喜剧演员，看另一个喜剧演员冷场会很有趣，但那只是因为那时你变成了观众。

sentences.en: The audience becomes the punchline to the joke, and you become the audience of watching the joke of an audience not getting a joke.
sentences.zh: 观众变成了笑话的包袱，而你变成了观看“观众没听懂笑话”这一笑话的观众。

sentences.en: And that's why when I was young, I kind of was very frustrated with Andy Kaufman's comedy because it was like Andy Kaufman is both the joke teller and the audience.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我年轻时对安迪·考夫曼的喜剧感到非常沮丧，因为安迪·考夫曼既是讲笑话的人，也是观众。

sentences.en: Like he – it is all about his reaction or his enjoyment of the audience's confusion.
sentences.zh: 他——这一切都关于他的反应，或者他享受观众的困惑。

sentences.en: I don't understand one thing.
sentences.zh: 我不明白一件事。

sentences.en: No, seriously.
sentences.zh: 不，说真的。

sentences.en: Why everyone is going boo on like the joke – when I told some of the jokes.
sentences.zh: 为什么每个人都在嘘——当我讲了一些笑话的时候。

sentences.en: And then when I don't want you to laugh, you're laughing.
sentences.zh: 然后当我不想让你们笑的时候，你们却在笑。

sentences.en: Like right now.
sentences.zh: 就像现在这样。

sentences.en: I don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我不明白。

sentences.en: Like, I get it.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我明白。

sentences.en: I get I get what you're saying, but I couldn't help it like it was it was a joke set up almoSt.
sentences.zh: 我明白你在说什么，但我忍不住，因为这几乎就是一个笑话的铺垫。

sentences.en: sense.

sentences.zh: 嗯，你是从已经设定的模式角度来考虑的。

sentences.zh: 他们设定了这样的模式：这些种子是最珍贵的东西，我们必须把它们

sentences.en: them in the safest possible place.
sentences.zh: 放在最安全的地方。

sentences.zh: 然后是对该模式的颠覆，也就是阿勒颇。

sentences.en: And you're right that you were laughing at the structure of that joke.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，你笑的是那个笑话的结构。

sentences.en: You were not laughing at the tragedy of what was going on at the time.
sentences.zh: 你并不是在嘲笑当时发生的悲剧。

sentences.en: It's a sense, you know, and it's individual for everyone.
sentences.zh: 这是一种感觉，你知道，对每个人来说都是独特的。

sentences.en: Elliot, I got to say, I love this book.
sentences.zh: 埃利奥特，我得说，我喜欢这本书。

sentences.zh: 而且你对过去几十年的喜剧有一个广泛的调查。

sentences.en: I was trying very hard to get a wide variety of people, comedy types, comedy mediuMs.
sentences.zh: 我非常努力地收集了各种各样的人、喜剧类型和喜剧媒介。

sentences.en: But even then, it's still just scratching the surface because there's so much.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，也只是触及了皮毛，因为内容太多了。

sentences.en: Comedy is so enormous.
sentences.zh: 喜剧太博大精深了。

sentences.zh: 其中投入了大量的手艺。

sentences.zh: 人。
